title: Economic Recovery Specialist-Employment& Labour Market Engagement
description: Danish Refugee Council, one of the world’s leading humanitarian NGOs, is currently looking for a qualified Economic Recovery Specialist – (Employement& Labour Market Engagement) for our operations in Dire Dawa, Ethiopia. Instruction for applicants: All applicants must upload a cover letter and an updated CV in English. Please ensure that your CV does not exceed three pages. Applications with CVs longer than the specified limit may not be considered Overall purpose of the role The Economic Recovery Specialist is the technical lead for the implementation of the economic recovery component of the Mixed Migration Programme, with a particular focus on employment pathways, market oriented apprenticeships, employer engagement, skills to employment linkages and labour market integration. The Specialist is responsible for designing, strengthening and quality assuring market oriented and protection sensitive economic pathways that enable migrants, returnees, transit populations, at risk youth and other vulnerable people on the move to access decent employment, paid apprenticeships, skills recognition and certification, and other viable income generating opportunities. The Specialist applies a Market Systems Development approach to identify and address the constraints that prevent people on the move from accessing and sustaining employment opportunities. Rather than relying on standardised livelihood packages, the Specialist ensures that programme support responds to participant skills, experience, aspirations, documentation status, mobility intentions and actual employer and labour market demand. The Specialist leads the technical development of employment and apprenticeship pathways, strengthens relationships with employers and other labour market actors, and ensures that programme interventions contribute to improved labour absorption and sustainable employment rather than creating parallel or permanently subsidised employment mechanisms. The Specialist works closely with Economic Recovery Officers, the Labour Mobility & Skills Recognition Officer, Protection, MEAL and Programme Management to ensure that participants are appropriately profiled, referred and supported across skills recognition, apprenticeships, employment and regular labour mobility pathways Your main duties and responsibilities will be: Labour Market Engagement, Employment Pathways & Private Sector Partnerships Lead analysis of high demand sectors, occupations, skills gaps, employer recruitment practices and barriers affecting migrants, returnees and at risk youth. Design market oriented employment pathways that respond to real labour demand and participant profiles. Build and manage strategic relationships with employers, industry associations, business networks and other labour market actors. Identify systemic barriers to recruitment, retention and advancement and develop practical responses with market actors. Facilitate linkages between participants and employers through authorised employment services and referral mechanisms. Strengthen approaches that enable employers and market actors to contribute placements, supervision, technical expertise, resources or other forms of support. Oversee placement, retention and transition tracking and use findings for continuous improvement. Market Oriented Paid Apprenticeships & Employer Incentives Lead the design, quality assurance and adaptive management of paid apprenticeship models in high demand sectors with realistic pathways into employment or self employment. Establish clear criteria for employer selection and ensure apprenticeships promote decent work, occupational safety, non discrimination and protection. Provide technical guidance on apprenticeship duration, workplace learning, supervision and transition planning. Design and oversee time bound, market aligned employer support or incentive mechanisms that increase labour absorption without creating long term subsidy dependence. Work with employers to address practical constraints related to recruitment, onboarding, supervision and retention, while encouraging them to contribute their own resources and expertise. Document lessons and continuously refine apprenticeship and incentive models based on employer and participant evidence. 3. Skills Recognition, Participant Placement & Employability Strengthen pathways linking prior informal skills to competency assessment, certification and employment, in close coordination with the Labour Mobility & Skills Recognition Officer, MoLS, CoC centres and TVETs. title: Community Outreach & Intervention Facilitator
description: Apply now Job no: 507276 Work type: Part-Time Location: Hybrid/Flexible Work Arrangement Categories: Dornsife School of Public Health Job Summary Community Outreach & Intervention Facilitators will support a five-year, NIH-funded research project focused on improving sleep, stress recovery, social connection, and wellbeing among men living in low resource communities in Philadelphia. This is a half-time (50% effort) position that combines community outreach and participant recruitment with delivery of a structured group-based health and wellbeing intervention. Working closely with the Principal Investigator, Program Manager, and research team, facilitators will help identify and engage potential participants, support screening and enrollment, maintain participant contact throughout the study, and facilitate or co-facilitate intervention sessions. Facilitators will receive training in recruitment, participant engagement, group facilitation, research ethics, intervention delivery, and study procedures. This position is grant-funded; employment is contingent upon the continued availability of those funds. Essential Functions Community Outreach and Recruitment Conduct community outreach and participant recruitment in partnership with community organizations and local stakeholders. Share study information with potential participants through community events, referrals, outreach activities, flyers, social media, and other approved recruitment strategies. Support responding to participant inquiries and clearly explain study participation. Support participant screening, enrollment, scheduling, reminders, and follow-up. Maintain accurate recruitment, outreach, and participant-tracking records. Build and maintain relationships with community organizations, referral partners, and potential participants. Work with the Program Manager and research team to identify and address recruitment and retention challenges. 40%% - Intervention Facilitation Facilitate or co-facilitate structured group intervention sessions using the project curriculum and facilitator guide. Create a welcoming, respectful, engaging, and nonjudgmental environment for participants. Guide conversations and activities related to sleep, stress, coping, relationships, social connection, masculinity, health, and wellbeing. Encourage participant engagement while respecting individual experiences, perspectives, and boundaries. Prepare for intervention sessions and participate in facilitator training, supervision, planning, and debriefing. Complete required attendance, session, fidelity, and participant-contact documentation. Follow established procedures for responding to participant concerns, distress, or requests for additional support. Maintain confidentiality and appropriate professional boundaries. 20%% - Project and Participant Support Maintain regular communication with participants to support engagement and retention. Participate in team meetings, trainings, supervision, and project-planning activities. Assist with community events and other study activities as needed. Communicate regularly with the Program Manager regarding recruitment progress, participant engagement, and implementation needs. Required Qualifications Experience working with community members through outreach, recruitment, education, service delivery, organizing, facilitation, or similar activities. Strong interpersonal and communication skills and the ability to build trust and rapport. Comfort speaking with individuals about research participation and health-related topics. Ability to facilitate or co-facilitate conversations about potentially sensitive topics. Strong reliability, organization, follow-through, and attention to detail. Ability to maintain confidentiality and follow structured research procedures. Ability to work collaboratively as part of a community-engaged research team. Availability for scheduled evening intervention sessions during active intervention periods. Preferred Qualifications Experience recruiting participants for research, health programs, community services, or similar initiatives. Experience facilitating groups, workshops, peer-support activities, or community programs. Experience working with Latino communities, men's health programs, or community-based organizations in Philadelphia. Spanish-language proficiency is welcomed but not required. Previous research experience is helpful but not required. Physical Demands Typically sitting at a desk/table Location Hybrid/Flexible Work Arrangement Additional Information This position is classified as Part time Non-Exempt, grade I. Compensation for this grade ranges from $21.71 to $32.57 per hour.
